stories.title: Vaishnav's Feedback
stories.description: Ajay mentions that their crew member Vaishnav gave feedback that Amit sometimes glosses over technical topics (curse of knowledge), prompting Amit to explain things better. This highlights the importance of respecting the listener.

stories.title: John Axon and the Radio Ballad
stories.description: Amit recounts the story of John Axon, a train driver who stayed on a runaway train to save lives. This was the subject of a 1957 radio ballad that pioneered using real interviews and sounds (show don't tell) instead of just narration.

stories.title: Son of the Family
stories.description: Amit mentions a Danish radio show about a musician who killed himself. The producers interviewed his family, and the raw emotion in their voices conveyed more than any narration could, illustrating the power of audio.

stories.title: Ram Guha Listening to Music
stories.description: Amit shares a story Ram Guha told on his podcast about lying in a dark room listening to Hindustani classical music, losing track of time until his wife found him. This illustrates the intimacy and depth possible in long-form podcasting.

stories.title: Ali Abdaal's Exponential Growth
stories.description: Amit cites Ali Abdaal's YouTube growth curve, which was flat for a long time before taking off exponentially. He uses this to advise creators to 'play the long game' and ignore numbers for the first two years.

core_ideas.description: Audio is the most intimate medium ('a voice in your head'). It allows for depth because listeners are often a captive audience (commuting, chores) and can process information faster than speech (listening at 2x speed).
Radio is structurally broad and shallow due to license fees and mass market imperatives. Podcasting is deep and intimate because the means of production are free and it can serve niches.
Don't talk down to the audience. Treat them as equals who are intelligent and curious. This builds a loyal relationship.
The only unique selling point you have is yourself. 'There is only one gap in the market: You aren't there.' Authenticity resonates more than market research.
Use action verbs and sound effects to convey meaning and character rather than relying on adjectives and abstract descriptions.
Perfection is the enemy of production. Start now, learn by doing, and iterate. 'Don't be a whiner, be a doer.'
Creators overestimate the short term and underestimate the long term. Ignore numbers for the first two years; growth is often exponential after a long flat period.

core_ideas.item: Loved by Few > Liked by Many
core_ideas.description: It is better to have 1,000 true fans who love your work and will support you than millions of shallow likes on social media.

jokes_and_cultural_references.text: Paul Simon on Poetry vs. Songs
jokes_and_cultural_references.context: Amit quotes Paul Simon explaining that poems are read multiple times but songs must work linearly on the first listen.
Amit quotes Neil Simon: 'There are two kinds of people in the world, the watchers and the doers, and the watchers sit around watching the doers do.'
